extracted.intended_audience: writers and readers of political pamphlets, pamphleteers, polemicists, and politically engaged public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for composing and critiquing political/polemical pamphlets: clarity of purpose, use of evidence, statistical honesty, tone, and logical consistency. Aimed at judging whether a pamphlet is informative, honest, and useful to public debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the piece's purpose and expected effects
rubrics_metrics.description: I will endeavor to state what this piece is; the purpose for which I take it to have been written; and the effects (supposing it should have any effect at all) it must necessarily produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good pamphlet (or a fair critique of one) should make explicit: what the work is, the author's purpose, and the likely consequences if its claims are accepted. Evaluators should ask whether the author has stated a clear intention and whether the claimed effects follow from the arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rehashing old controversies and needless repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments ten times repeated, a thousand times answered before, are here repeated again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assemble a 'farrago' of topics that merely recycle well-worn complaints without adding new insight. Repeating previously answered arguments or commonplaces (e.g., 'decay of trade', 'increase of taxes') bloats a piece without increasing its weight or usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use paradoxes or barren truths that generate no conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Paradoxes which affront common sense, and uninteresting barren truths which generate no conclusion, are thrown in to augment unwieldy bulk, without adding anything to weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inserting clever-sounding paradoxes or trivial facts that don't lead to a meaningful conclusion. Every claim should contribute to a coherent case; otherwise it is filler that undermines the work's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contradictions; reconcile conflicting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Contradictions are set staring one another in the face, without even an attempt to reconcile them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must not assert mutually incompatible positions. If different claims imply tension, acknowledge and resolve them rather than leaving contradictory statements side by side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match tone and composition to the purpose; avoid sermonizing for private advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the composition, it bears a striking and whimsical resemblance to a funeral sermon... well stored with pious frauds, and, like most discourses of the sort, much better calculated for the private advantage of the preacher than the edification of the hearers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone should serve the public purpose: avoid doleful, preachy, or manipulative styles ('pious frauds') that appear designed to flatter or benefit the author rather than to inform or edify readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make meaning clear; don't obfuscate to hide design
rubrics_metrics.description: The author has indeed so involved his subject, that it is frequently far from being easy to comprehend his meaning. It is happy for the public that it is never difficult to fathom his design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of expression is essential. Obscure or over-involved prose that masks an obvious design (e.g., partisan or manipulative intent) is a fault. Readers should be able to understand both the claims and the author's motives without decoding opaque language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not arbitrarily dominate or manipulate facts to fit a narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Aided by the arbitrary dominion he assumes over fact...the apparent intention of this author is to draw the most aggravated, hideous and deformed picture of the state of this country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not exercise 'arbitrary dominion' over facts—selecting, twisting, or suppressing evidence to create a grotesque picture. Fair use of facts requires honest presentation and proportional interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute causes correctly; avoid misattribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Had he attributed our misfortunes to their true cause...the complaint had been just, and might have been useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct causal analysis is crucial. Misassigning causes (blaming constitutional weakness rather than policy failures, for example) makes a complaint unjust and useless. Writers should trace causes carefully and distinguish structural from contingent factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fear-mongering and using alarm to push partisan remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The author is in hopes, that, when we are fallen into a fanatical terror for the national salvation, we shall then be ready to throw ourselves...into the hands of the most pretending and forward undertaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not manufacture or exaggerate dangers to induce readers to accept particular leaders or solutions. Appeals to panic that serve to funnel support to 'pretending' actors are manipulative and disqualify the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure methods are justified by the purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: That purpose ought to be a wonderfully good one, to warrant the methods he has taken to compass it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhetorical or evidentiary methods that would be questionable require proportionately weighty ends to be defensible. Examine whether the means (e.g., selective evidence, rhetorical excesses) match the importance of the goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on principles, not only on isolated cases
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall follow the author closely...not for the sake of the particular measures which he discusses...but for the sake of the principles of war, peace, trade, and finances. These principles are of infinite moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debate should elevate and test general principles underlying specific policies. Evaluators should ask whether an argument engages the governing principles, since those will recur across future situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check whether conclusions follow from premises; beware sweeping generalizations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the facts and reasonings in this piece are admitted, it is all over with us...It is impossible, if this state of things be credited abroad, that we can have any alliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the narrative's premises legitimately imply its dire conclusions. Beware of sweeping inferences made from limited or contested premises; test each inferential step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accurate and appropriately chosen metrics and data
rubrics_metrics.description: I take the imports from, and not the exports to, these conquests, as the measure of the advantages which we derived from them...Our export entry does not comprehend the greatest trade we carry on with any of the West India islands...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the data and metrics that actually capture the phenomenon under discussion. For trade, customs imports may better reflect value than exports in some contexts; select measures that reflect economic reality rather than convenient numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simplistic accounting and inappropriate balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: It is therefore quite ridiculous, to strike a balance merely on the face of an excess of imports and exports, in that commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on simplistic import/export balances where they misrepresent the true position (e.g., omit non-recorded trades, remittances, or services). Use the correct accounting framework for the question at hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check claims against available evidence; do not ignore contradictory data
rubrics_metrics.description: This he asserts roundly and boldly, and without the least concern; although it cost no more than a single glance of the eye upon his own margin to see the full refutation of this assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making empirical claims, authors must check their data carefully, and cannot blithely ignore information that contradicts their assertions. A single glance at the cited sources should reveal obvious counter-evidence if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not misapply averages or inappropriate statistical summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: His method of stating a medium of six years of war, and six years of peace, to decide this question, is altogether unfair...one may lay it down as a maxim, that an average estimate of an object in a steady course of rising or of falling, must in its nature be an unfair one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averages can mislead when applied to trending (non-stationary) series. Avoid comparing blunt multi-year means across periods with different trajectories; choose statistics that respect the time-series behavior and avoid averaging away trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cherry-picking timeframes to favor a thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: He had his reasons for stopping short at the preceding year. It would have appeared, had he proceeded farther, that our tonnage was in a course of uniform augmentation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not select start/end points or short windows that make a trend look worse (or better) than it is. Test robustness across longer spans and alternative cutoffs to detect cherry-picking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide relevance: ensure facts/records are applied to the purpose they are produced for
rubrics_metrics.description: They are accompanied with facts and records, which may seem of a little more weight. I trust, however, that the facts of this author will be as far from bearing the touchstone, as his arguments. ...they are all either false or fallaciously applied; or not in the least to the purpose for which they are produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gathered facts must be relevant and properly applied. Presenting documents or figures that do not actually support the asserted point is deceptive; evidence must be tied explicitly and legitimately to the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult proper authorities and experience when asserting operational claims
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not have been amiss if he had consulted the public experience, and our commanders, concerning the absolute certainty of those conquests on which he is pleased to found our security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making claims about feasibility (military conquest, economic outcomes, etc.), cite practitioners and empirical experience. Do not assert 'certainty' without consulting those with operational knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stating obvious truisms as deep analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: They contain nothing more than a commonplace against war; the easiest of all topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from dressing up banalities (e.g., 'war is expensive, peace desirable') as novel insights. Analysis should go beyond truisms to add explanatory depth or new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be numerically accurate; slovenliness in accounting is inexcusable
rubrics_metrics.description: In matters of account, however, this want of care is not excusable; and the difference between neutral nations entirely engrossing our navigation, and being only subsidiary to a vastly augmented trade, makes a most material difference to his argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precision in numerical claims and accounting matters is essential. Sloppiness or inaccuracy in figures undermines credibility and can fatally skew conclusions; double-check calculations and contextualize numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret trends and changes (not just snapshots) to assess future expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The fair account of the matter is this...our trade had increased to so astonishing a degree in 1761...I have done fairly, and even very moderately, in taking this year, and not his average, as the standard of what might be expected in future, had the war continued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forecasting or judging potential future states, consider trend direction, evolution across years, and whether a given year is representative. Use appropriate standards for projecting likely continuation or reversal.
